opening_message:
Ticket 1: Keith Mclaughlin (employee ID E032) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E032.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Keith Mclaughlin (E032) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, write is within policy (admin would require owning role). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security check: Keith Mclaughlin (E032) is a contractor with basic security training per Security DB (note that an earlier note listed full_time, but Security DB shows contractor). Contractors with basic training are limited to read; write requires advanced training. Requested write, so recommend read.
reason: The Security agent's note reports a direct database lookup showing Keith Mclaughlin (E032) is a contractor with basic security training, and explicitly flags a discrepancy with the earlier HR note listing full_time. Under policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training. With basic training, the maximum allowed is read, and requested write exceeds that, so grant the maximum of read. Granting write would exceed the contractor's permitted level, so read is the appropriate decision.
